clue.text: Dam childishly associated with large beaver perhaps

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, and a child's word for mother is mamma
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A nursery tale in which a beaver's mother is described in baby talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaver is one example of a warm-blooded furry animal that suckles its young.

clue.text: Block trouble outside Nevada

indicators.note: outside says the trouble word wraps around the state abbreviation

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
NV is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Nevada

explanation.surface: A news item about difficulties surrounding a building plot in the Nevada desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's anvil is a heavy iron block on which metal is hammered.

clue.text: Lisa perhaps, right in fashion like a queen

parts.note: Mona is the name that goes with Lisa in Leonardo's famous portrait
chic means stylish or in fashion

explanation.surface: Lisa, perhaps a fashionable dresser, carries herself like a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchic describes anything relating to a sovereign ruler, such as a queen.

clue.text: A row following the French introduction

indicators.note: following places the A and row pieces after the French article

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a row is a noisy din

explanation.surface: A dispute coming after the French opening remarks of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is a preliminary passage or remark that serves as an opening.

clue.text: Bid competitively totally in control of clubs

indicators.note: in control of suggests one piece holding the other, so the clubs letter sits within

parts.note: overall means in total, totally
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A bridge player bidding aggressively because they hold total command of the club suit.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, to overcall is to bid after an opponent has opened the bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge an overcall is a bid made over an opponent's opening, competing for the contract.

clue.text: Elderly person given a prod — gone senile unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An elderly person is nudged awake, sadly having lost their faculties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges A PROD GONE SENILE; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British term for a retired person drawing a state pension, so an older person.

clue.text: Round university grinned inanely without stopping

indicators.note: Round says the mixed letters go around the university letter
inanely means foolishly, so the letters are mixed up senselessly

explanation.surface: Someone grinning foolishly as they make a tour of the university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inanely' rearranges GRINNED, and 'Round' puts that mixture around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring lasts on and on, continuing without a break or stopping.

clue.text: Maybe Arabs' young guns

definitions.meaning: young male horses, of which Arabs are one breed
revolvers made by the Colt firearms company

explanation.definitionFit: Young male horses and a famous make of revolver share this one word.

clue.text: Laird's family not first to get fit of depression

indicators.note: not first removes the opening letter of the family word

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
a downer is a spell of low spirits

explanation.surface: A Scottish laird's kin are not the first to fall into gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish owner of an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the Scottish name for a proprietor of a landed estate.

clue.text: Finished outside haven in storm without favour

indicators.note: outside says the finished word wraps around the mixed letters

parts.note: finished means ended

indicators.note: in storm suggests being tossed about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A ship's voyage finished outside a harbour during a gale, without favourable winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in storm' scrambles the harbour word, and 'outside' places the finished word around the result; 'favour' in the surface suggests a wind, not partiality.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-handed means impartial, treating all sides fairly without favour.

clue.text: Bond's spoken of wild cat

indicators.note: spoken of says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: bonds are ties or links

explanation.surface: James Bond is said to have talked about a ferocious feline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but a bond is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears and a short tail.

clue.text: Make slight sharp sound eating noisily

parts.note: to slur is to slight or disparage
a ping is a short sharp ringing noise

explanation.surface: Instructions on producing a faint, high-pitched noise while having a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slurping is sucking food or drink in noisily, as with soup.

clue.text: Take some euros to visit Russian port

indicators.note: Take some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice for a traveller to pack some currency before a trip to a Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostov-on-Don is a major Russian river port near the Sea of Azov.

clue.text: King Henry the First has returned outside

indicators.note: outside says the reversed word goes around the initial
returned says the word has is read backwards
the First takes just the initial letter of Henry

explanation.surface: King Henry I has come back from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns HAS into SAH, which goes 'outside' H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shah was the title of the king of Iran.

clue.text: Executed heretic from central European country

parts.note: executed on the gallows means hung
an Arian was a follower of the heretic Arius

explanation.surface: A heretic from central Europe being put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungarian means coming from Hungary, a landlocked nation in central Europe.

clue.text: Liking piano to utterly delight

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to enchant is to delight completely

explanation.surface: A fondness for the piano that completely charms the listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong taste or inclination for something.

clue.text: Aristocratic students given drugs?

parts.note: someone given drugs is high
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: A question whether upper-crust pupils have been supplied with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: High-class means of superior social standing, as aristocrats are.

clue.text: Salt kept in tree's highest point

indicators.note: kept in says the salt formula is held inside the tree

parts.note: a pine is a tree
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: Salt stored inside the topmost part of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: NACL is sodium chloride, the chemist's name for table salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the peak or summit, the highest point of something.

clue.text: Fighting sloth

definitions.meaning: read as two words, engaged in combat
laziness, a failure to do anything

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word means engaged in battle; whole it means idleness.

clue.text: Banking system to fix returns — zero

indicators.note: returns says the fixing word is read backwards

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly
O resembles the figure zero

explanation.surface: A banking network rigged so that it yields nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RIG into GIR. Giro is a British system of bank transfers.
explanation.definitionFit: Giro is a system of direct credit transfer between bank or post office accounts.

clue.text: Outside south-east, be mother superior type

indicators.note: Outside says the pouring word wraps around the compass letters

parts.note: to be mother is the British idiom for pouring the tea

explanation.surface: A Mother Superior stands outside a convent in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the person who serves tea is said to 'be mother'.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur is an affected person who puts on airs of superiority.

clue.text: Woolly surface with relation to small cloth

parts.note: nap is the raised fibre on the surface of woollen fabric
kin are relations

explanation.surface: A fuzzy fabric shared with a relative, cut into a small cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a small square of cloth used at table.

clue.text: Broadcast means to enter vehicle with military associations

indicators.note: Broadcast says the phrase is heard over the air, not spelt

parts.note: a car key is how you get into a car

explanation.surface: A radio report on how soldiers get into an army vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the phrase sounds just like the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is the dull brownish colour of army uniforms, so it carries military associations.

clue.text: Warship to press young man rounding cape

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
C is the map abbreviation for cape
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A warship pressganging a young man as it sails around a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironclad was a nineteenth-century warship armoured with iron plates.

clue.text: Clothes-horse more attractive without top

indicators.note: without top removes the first letter of the down answer's word

parts.note: fairer means prettier, more attractive

explanation.surface: A fashion model, prettier than the rest, going topless.
explanation.walkthrough: A clothes-horse is a folding frame for drying laundry, not a fashion-conscious person.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a frame on which washing is hung to dry, also called a clothes-horse.

clue.text: Serve a famous opera

parts.note: to serve is to help or aid

explanation.surface: An instruction to offer up a well-known musical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's celebrated opera set in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: May Trotter get a support? — he famously crashed one of these

definitions.text: he famously crashed one of these

parts.note: may and can both express permission
Del Boy Trotter is the wheeler-dealer in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Asking whether a TV character may be given some kind of prop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a famous Only Fools and Horses scene, Del Boy and his family send a stately-home chandelier crashing to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom's fallen light fitting is a branched holder of lights, close kin to a candlestick holder.

clue.text: Mastermind in Greene novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal genius appears in a Graham Greene novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a plot is to contrive or mastermind it.

clue.text: A queen wearing red beads

indicators.note: wearing says the red word is put on around the queen pieces

parts.note: rosy means pinkish red
R is the abbreviation for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A monarch dressed in scarlet with a string of beads.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a string of prayer beads used by Catholics.
